A quiet outdoor room at the center of the home.

props.alt: Fictional courtyard study: pale brick, oak-framed openings and a planted gravel court

props.html: The study places everyday rooms around a sheltered court. Openings face the planting, bringing a changing view and borrowed light into the home. The aim is a close relationship between the rooms people use most and the space outside.

props.text: Light from more than one side.

props.html: The courtyard creates an additional edge for windows and doors. Deep reveals frame the view while giving each opening a sense of shelter.
Pale brick forms the enclosure. Oak marks the places where the building opens. Gravel and low planting keep the court informal and usable.
The court can hold a morning chair, an open door, or a view from the table. The proposal begins with those modest uses rather than a formal entrance sequence.
This narrative and the AI-generated scene describe a fictional design study. They do not document construction, technical performance, or a completed commission.

pages.desc: A demonstration architecture practice focused on homes and shared places.
pages.name: About

props.html: Common Ground is a fictional architecture practice exploring homes, existing buildings, and places a neighborhood can share.

A useful starting point is the place itself: the direction of the light, the parts worth keeping, and the way people move through a day. Those observations can become a clear brief before they become a drawing.
A project starts with the people who will use it. A conversation about routines, constraints, and expectations gives the design something concrete to answer.
Existing fabric can carry useful space, material, and character. The sample studies ask where keeping a building can be more valuable than starting again.
Plans, material samples, and plain-language notes should help a client understand what is proposed and what still needs to be resolved.
For template owners: replace this demonstration practice description with your own team, experience, and professional information. No people, registrations, or credentials are implied here.
Tell us what is there now and what you would like to change.

pages.title: The practice — Common Ground

pages.desc: Example architecture service scopes for a residential and adaptive reuse practice.
pages.name: Services

props.text: From a first question to a clear brief.

props.html: The following scopes are examples for this demonstration practice. Actual services, fees, appointments, and responsibilities should be agreed for each project.
Explore whether the building or site can support the uses you have in mind. Begin with the brief, existing information, and the constraints that need further investigation.
A working brief, a record of key constraints, and options for the next stage.
Consider how rooms, light, and outdoor space can work together. The study may begin with an existing house or with a new arrangement on a site.
An outline spatial proposal, a material direction, and the decisions requiring specialist advice.
Explore a new use for a retained building. Pay attention to what can stay, how people enter and circulate, and what makes a shared room useful.
A reuse strategy, an outline layout, and a list of technical questions for the project team.
Bring the location, photographs or existing drawings if available, the uses you have in mind, and any known constraints. A rough sense of timing and budget helps frame a useful discussion.
